sn12.40:1.2: “Bhikkhus, what one intends, and what one plans, and whatever one has a tendency towards: this becomes a basis for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.40:1.3: When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn12.40:1.4: When consciousness is established and has come to growth, there is inclination.
sn12.40:1.5: When there is inclination, there is coming and going.
sn12.40:1.6: When there is coming and going, there is passing away and being reborn.
sn12.40:1.7: When there is passing away and being reborn, future birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair come to be.
sn12.40:1.8: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.40:2.1: “If, bhikkhus, one does not intend, and one does not plan, but one still has a tendency towards something, this becomes a basis for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.40:2.2: When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishing of consciousness….
sn12.40:2.7: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.40:3.1: “But, bhikkhus, when one does not intend, and one does not plan, and one does not have a tendency towards anything, no basis exists for the maintenance of consciousness.
sn12.40:3.2: When there is no basis, there is no support for the establishing of consciousness.
sn12.40:3.3: When consciousness is unestablished and does not come to growth, there is no inclination.
sn12.40:3.4: When there is no inclination, there is no coming and going.
sn12.40:3.5: When there is no coming and going, there is no passing away and being reborn.
sn12.40:3.6: When there is no passing away and being reborn, future birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair cease.
sn12.40:3.7: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
